'''Fussballclub Zürich''', commonly abbreviated to '''FC Zürich''' or simply '''FCZ''', is a professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Zurich]], Switzerland. The club was founded in 1896 and has won the [[Swiss Super League]] thirteen times and the [[Swiss Cup]] ten times. Their most recent titles are the [[2021–22 Swiss Super League|2022 Swiss Super League]] and the [[2017-18 Swiss Cup|2018 Swiss Cup]]. The club plays its home games at the [[Letzigrund]], which has a capacity of around 26,000 for league games<ref>{{cite web|title=Das Stadion Letzigrund in Zahlen und Fakten|url=https://www.stadionletzigrund.ch/de/zahlenfakten|website=stadionletzigrund.ch|access-date=17 August 2021|archive-date=9 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509232557/https://www.stadionletzigrund.ch/de/zahlenfakten|url-status=live}}</ref> and which it shares with city rivals [[Grasshopper Club Zurich]].

FC Zürich is the only Swiss team to have reached the semi-finals of the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] more than once. This happened in 1964 and 1977 when the competition was played in its original format. FC Zürich co-founder, first captain and honorary member was [[Joan Gamper]], who grew up in Zurich and later moved to [[Catalonia]], founding [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] there in 1899. Since the 1960s, FC Zürich plays in all-white, which is one of the city's colours.

The women's club, [[FC Zürich Frauen]], compete in the [[Swiss Women's Super League]]. They are the most successful club in Switzerland with 22 championship titles and multiple [[UEFA Women's Champions League|Champions League]] participations. The team's roots originate from the first Swiss women's football club, DFC Zürich.<ref>{{cite web |author=Saro Pepe |title=Football for all – but only for the last 50 years |url=https://blog.nationalmuseum.ch/en/2018/09/50-years-of-womens-football-in-switzerland/ |access-date=17 August 2021 |website=nationalmuseum.ch |archive-date=12 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240112130219/https://blog.nationalmuseum.ch/en/2018/09/50-years-of-womens-football-in-switzerland/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
